editorial:
Imagine a loud, guitar-playing country boy who knows exactly how to play the crowd to get what he wants. That is Lonesome Rhodes. You get to watch him go from a small-town troublemaker to a massive TV star who can basically pick the next president. Along the way, you meet Marcia, a smart city girl who thinks she can help him, but she quickly finds out that Lonesome is way more dangerous and clever than she ever imagined. It feels like a wild ride through the early days of television where anyone with a loud voice could become a god.

What really hits home is the acting. You can almost feel the energy when Lonesome is talking to thousands of people. The pacing is tight, and it is scary how much this movie feels like it could happen today with social media. The only downside is that some of the 1950s dialogue feels a bit slow, but the drama makes up for it. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about power and fame. If you can, grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection to see the old sets in detail, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Lonesome tries to control the government too much. He gets caught in a lie and loses his power over the public. In the end, you see him stripped of his fame and sent back to where he started. He ends up right back in a small-town jail. It shows that while he could trick the world for a while, his ego eventually caused his own downfall.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about fame and power.
